baselines.B0: prior-season per-game value of the same outcome
baselines.B1: ridge on prior per-game targets, receptions, yards, games played, TE flag

decision_rule.PROMISING: relative MAE improvement >= 1% over the baseline AND the Bonferroni-adjusted CI of the paired difference excludes 0 AND better in >= 2 of the 3 test seasons
decision_rule.REJECTED: relative improvement < 0.25% OR the CI lies entirely on the wrong side

spec.football_rationale: Targets follow routes run, how often a player is the first read and where he lines up; production-only baselines mix role with luck and with a one-off team context. Role is closer to the cause of volume.
spec.hypothesis: Route participation, targets per route, first-read/designed-target share, alignment mix and XFP of season N-1 improve prediction of season N per-game targets, receptions and receiving yards beyond the player's own prior per-game production.
spec.leakage: features from season N-1 only; season N file used as outcome only
spec.metric: mean absolute error (primary), RMSE and Spearman (secondary)
sources: Fantasy Points receiving_advanced, receiving_basic 2021-2025 (retrospective, regular season)
spec.title: Prior-season role profile -> next-season receiving volume and yards (WR/TE)
spec.unit: WR/TE player-season pair (N-1 -> N) with >= 8 games in both seasons

baselines.B1: ridge on prior FP/G (and TD/G), games, position flags

decision_rule.PROMISING: relative MAE improvement >= 1% over the baseline AND the Bonferroni-adjusted CI of the paired difference excludes 0 AND better in >= 2 of the 3 test seasons
decision_rule.REJECTED: relative improvement < 0.25% OR the CI lies entirely on the wrong side

spec.football_rationale: Results include touchdown and efficiency variance that does not persist; opportunity volume does.
spec.hypothesis: XFP/G of season N-1 adds to FP/G of N-1 in predicting FP/G of N (regression toward opportunity); XTD/G adds to TD/G in predicting next-season TD/G.
spec.metric: mean absolute error (primary), RMSE and Spearman (secondary)
spec.title: Expected fantasy points / expected TDs vs actual: does opportunity predict next season better than results?
spec.unit: WR/TE/RB player-season pair with >= 8 games in both seasons

baselines.B1: ridge on prior-season per-game targets/receptions/yards (nflverse weekly) + TE flag
baselines.B2: B1 + mean of the player's earlier weeks this season (prior average if none), number of earlier appearances

decision_rule.PROMISING: relative MAE improvement >= 1% over the baseline AND the Bonferroni-adjusted CI of the paired difference excludes 0 AND better in >= 2 of the 3 test seasons
decision_rule.REJECTED: relative improvement < 0.25% OR the CI lies entirely on the wrong side

spec.football_rationale: Early in a season rolling usage is a handful of games; role history is a better estimate of the true role. Later the sample dominates.
spec.hypothesis: Prior-season role features (E1 set) improve weekly target/reception/yard predictions beyond prior-season per-game averages AND the player's own rolling in-season usage, most strongly in weeks 1-4 and fading as in-season evidence accumulates.
spec.leakage: prior-season features only; rolling means use weeks strictly before the target week
spec.limitations: conditions on the player appearing in the weekly stats; does not model who plays
spec.metric: mean absolute error (primary), RMSE and Spearman (secondary)
spec.multiple_testing: Bonferroni over 3 outcomes for the primary weeks 1-4 bucket (98.33% CI); other buckets descriptive only
spec.title: Weekly application: do prior-season role features add to what GOING already knows in-season (rolling usage)?
spec.unit: WR/TE player-week (regular season weeks 1-18) with prior-season >= 8 games and Fantasy Points prior features; only players who recorded stats that week

baselines.D1: D0 + man-vs-zone advantage + opponent man rate (main effects)

spec.challenger: D2 = D1 + advantage x opponent man rate

decision_rule.PROMISING: relative MAE improvement >= 1% over the baseline AND the Bonferroni-adjusted CI of the paired difference excludes 0 AND better in >= 2 of the 3 test seasons
decision_rule.REJECTED: relative improvement < 0.25% OR the CI lies entirely on the wrong side

definitions.advantage: (Man YPRR - Zone YPRR) * min(1, Man RTE/100), zero when Man RTE < 40 or Zone RTE < 100
definitions.opponent_man_rate: opponent prior-season Man/Zone MAN % centred and scaled over teams in that season

spec.football_rationale: Coverage shell changes who wins routes; the interaction is the matchup, not either part alone.
spec.hypothesis: A receiver who produced better per route against man than zone (prior season) outperforms his baseline more when the opponent played more man coverage (prior season); the interaction term improves weekly receiving-yard prediction beyond main effects.
spec.leakage: prior-season coverage and receiver splits only
spec.metric: mean absolute error (primary), RMSE and Spearman (secondary)
spec.title: Matchup interaction: receiver man-coverage advantage x opponent man-coverage rate
spec.unit: as E3 for seasons 2023-2025 (the 2021 coverage scale is not comparable, so opponent coverage uses 2022+ prior seasons)

baselines.B1: ridge on prior overall pass rate

spec.challenger: C5 = B1 + neutral, leading and trailing pass rates

decision_rule.PROMISING: relative MAE improvement >= 1% over the baseline AND the Bonferroni-adjusted CI of the paired difference excludes 0 AND better in >= 2 of the 3 test seasons
decision_rule.REJECTED: relative improvement < 0.25% OR the CI lies entirely on the wrong side

spec.football_rationale: Overall pass rate mixes the offense's preference with how often it was ahead or behind.
spec.hypothesis: Neutral/leading/trailing pass rates of season N-1 predict season N overall pass rate better than the overall pass rate alone.
spec.limitations: about 96 test team-seasons: low power, so INCONCLUSIVE is the expected honest outcome unless the effect is large
spec.metric: mean absolute error (primary), RMSE and Spearman (secondary)
spec.title: Team pass-rate persistence: does game-script-split pass rate beat overall pass rate?

decision_rule.PROMISING: relative MAE improvement >= 1% over the baseline AND the Bonferroni-adjusted CI of the paired difference excludes 0 AND better in >= 2 of the 3 test seasons
decision_rule.REJECTED: relative improvement < 0.25% OR the CI lies entirely on the wrong side

spec.football_rationale: Same as E1; fewer degrees of freedom.
spec.hypothesis: E1 failed in the first test seasons and recovered in the last, the pattern of an over-parameterised model trained on ~100 rows. A compact set (targets per route run, route participation, first-read share) may add to the production baseline without that overfit.
spec.limitations: POST-HOC: designed after seeing E1 on the same seasons. Exploratory only: a PROMISING result is capped at NEEDS PROSPECTIVE DATA and may not support promotion.
spec.metric: mean absolute error (primary), RMSE and Spearman (secondary)
spec.title: EXPLORATORY follow-up to E1: three compact role features instead of fifteen

spec.champion: production window mean: last 12 regular-season appearances (QB: verified starts), min 5, 80% current-season / 20% earlier-season weights (reconstruction validated against the 2026 frozen projection_mean: 91% exact for receptions and receiving yards)

comparators.W1: equal weights over the window (no season weighting)
comparators.W3: learned shrinkage: (k*current_mean + c*prior_mean)/(k+c), c from the grid [0.5..40] chosen on TRAIN seasons only per market
comparators.W4: ridge on current mean, prior mean, k, k=0 flag, prior games

decision_rule.PROMISING: relative MAE improvement >= 1% over the comparison base AND the Bonferroni-adjusted CI of the paired difference excludes 0 AND better in >= 2 of 3 test seasons
decision_rule.REJECTED (v2): the adjusted CI excludes a gain of 1% (or lies entirely on the wrong side)

spec.football_rationale: One or two games are a noisy read of a role; early in a season the earlier seasons contain most of the real information, and by midseason the current role dominates. The 80/20 rule jumps to 80% after a single game.
spec.hypothesis: The production policy gives 80% of the weight to the current season's games however few there are; a blend whose prior strength is learned (prior games count as c pseudo-games) predicts weekly outcomes better, mainly in the first six weeks.
spec.leakage: window = games strictly before the target week
spec.limitations: tests the projected MEAN; no historical prop lines exist, so no ROI. The Poisson/lognormal distribution layer and the injury adjustments are not reconstructed.
spec.metric: MAE of the projected mean (primary), Poisson log score (secondary)
spec.outcomes: the weekly stat of each market
spec.population: player appearances 2021-2025 with a production-ready window (>= 5 games; QBs: verified starters only); markets receptions, rec_yds, rec_tds, rush_yds, rush_tds, atd, pass_yds, pass_tds by position
spec.primary_comparison: W3 vs W0, weeks 1-6, per market (8 markets, Bonferroni 99.375% CI)
spec.secondary: all weeks; W1 and W4; MAE by number of current games; Poisson log score for count markets
sources: nflverse weekly player stats, snap counts, schedules 2019-2025
spec.title: Dynamic blend of prior and current-season usage vs the production 80/20 policy

spec.champion: production window mean: last 12 regular-season appearances (QB: verified starts), min 5, 80% current-season / 20% earlier-season weights (reconstruction validated against the 2026 frozen projection_mean: 91% exact for receptions and receiving yards)

decision_rule.PROMISING: relative MAE improvement >= 1% over the comparison base AND the Bonferroni-adjusted CI of the paired difference excludes 0 AND better in >= 2 of 3 test seasons
decision_rule.REJECTED (v2): the adjusted CI excludes a gain of 1% (or lies entirely on the wrong side)

spec.football_rationale: Expected points describe the quality of touches (location, depth, down) that raw production and counts miss.
spec.hypothesis: Expected-opportunity information adds to the Champion's mean; Fantasy Points XFP adds something beyond ffopportunity (which GOING already has).
spec.leakage: Fantasy Points features are prior-season only; ffopportunity current-season values use earlier weeks only
spec.limitations: Fantasy Points XFP exists only as a prior-season total (no weekly history before 2026), ffopportunity has weekly values; a fair test of timing advantage is the MEO row.

models.MEO: MEOP + ffopportunity current-season rolling expected value + games count (the in-season advantage ffopportunity has)
models.MEOP: M0 + ffopportunity prior-season per-game expected value of the market stat (apples-to-apples with MFP)
models.MFP: M0 + Fantasy Points prior-season XFP/G, XTD/G
models.MV: M0 + raw volume (Champion-window targets/g or carries/g)

spec.multiple_testing: Bonferroni over 5 markets x 4 comparisons = 20 (99.75% CI)
spec.population: appearances 2022-2025 with a ready Champion window and available prior-season Fantasy Points efficiency and ffopportunity rows (complete-case, identical across models)
primary_comparisons: MEOFP vs MEOP (does Fantasy Points add beyond ffopportunity?)
spec.title: Fantasy Points XFP vs ffopportunity expected points vs raw volume, each against the Champion

spec.champion: production window mean: last 12 regular-season appearances (QB: verified starts), min 5, 80% current-season / 20% earlier-season weights (reconstruction validated against the 2026 frozen projection_mean: 91% exact for receptions and receiving yards)

decision_rule.PROMISING: relative MAE improvement >= 1% over the comparison base AND the Bonferroni-adjusted CI of the paired difference excludes 0 AND better in >= 2 of 3 test seasons
decision_rule.REJECTED (v2): the adjusted CI excludes a gain of 1% (or lies entirely on the wrong side)

spec.football_rationale: Carries follow role and game script; yards per carry are mostly noise and regress; goal-line TDs follow role.
spec.hypothesis: Bell-cow role shares and role stability predict weekly carries/rushing yards beyond Champion + raw volume; efficiency metrics (success, stuff, contact yards) do not.
spec.leakage: prior-season features only; share statistics from games before the target week
spec.limitations: carries are not a market GOING prices, but they drive the markets that it does

models.M0: Champion mean of the outcome + RB-only constant
models.R1: MV + Fantasy Points bell-cow block (snap %, carry share %, target share %, XFP share %) from the prior season
models.R2: MV + Fantasy Points advanced rushing block (success %, stuff %, contact yards/att, missed tackles/att, explosive run %, yards before contact/att, zone share)
models.R3: MV + role stability from nflverse (window mean, window SD and current-vs-prior change of the team carry share)
models.R4: MV + ffopportunity prior-season expected rushing yards and TDs per game

spec.multiple_testing: Bonferroni over 3 outcomes x 4 blocks = 12 (99.58% CI)
spec.population: RB appearances 2022-2025 with a ready Champion window and the prior-season Fantasy Points rows needed by each block (complete-case per comparison)
spec.title: Rushing / bell-cow: role share, advanced rushing efficiency, role stability and expected opportunity over Champion plus raw volume
